What changed (text excerpt): Added: + Spring/summer online debut planned for historical York County records + ALFRED, Maine – In May 1835, Ivory R. Hatch, who lived in the town of Wells, was unhappy with the result of an interaction with the town concerning a portion of his land. Wells selectmen had undertaken to lay out a road – an important decision at a time when there weren’t many roads. The new road, to be 3 rods, or 49.5 feet wide, was to be built on several portions of privately held land – including 72 rods, or 1,188 feet – of Hatch’s property. “Aggrieved,” in the amount of + Tammy L Wells + 1 day ago + 4 min read Removed: - Seeing history, up close - While people drive by the 1806 York County Court House in Alfred every day, many may have never been inside, and fewer still may know how much history lives in this county-owned building. - Tammy L Wells - Oct 2, 2025 - 6 min read
